slides.heading: Minimum Area Rectangle
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Minimum Area Rectangle, a very hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Smallest-area axis-aligned rectangle whose 4 corners are in the point set, else 0.
Treat each pair as a diagonal and check the other two corners.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Smallest-area axis-aligned rectangle whose 4 corners are in the point set, else 0. Treat each pair as a diagonal and check the other two corners.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Any two points that could be opposite corners determine the other two, so check them in a hash set.
slides.narration: Any two points that could be opposite corners determine the other two, so check them in a hash set.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Pairs as diagonals + hash set → O(n²)
slides.narration: Checking all groups of four is n to the fourth. Treating pairs as diagonals with a hash set is quadratic.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each pair with different x and y, check the other corners
slides.narration: Step by step. First, put points in a set. Second, for each pair with different x and y, check the other corners. Third, track the smallest area.
